scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which falls just outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Jin Chen and I'm 42. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Jin. I'm sorry to hear about the trouble with the timing of this charge while you were away. I'd be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide the email address associated with your account and the last four digits of the payment method used?
Sure, the email is j.chen@email.com and the card ends in 4492.

Thank you, Jin. I have located your account. I see the cancellation was processed on the 34th day prior to today. Our 'Standard Billing and Refund Policy (Section 4.2)' strictly limits automated refunds to a 30-day window from the transaction date. However, given your account history is in good standing, I can request a one-time exception for you.
That would be a huge help, thank you. I really didn't intend to let it slide this long.

I completely understand, travel can certainly make keeping up with notifications difficult. I have submitted the request to our billing department for a manual override. I've also applied a $10 courtesy credit to your account for the inconvenience. You should see the refund processed to your card ending in 4492 within 3-5 business days.
Oh, that's incredibly kind of you. Thank you so much for the help and the credit!
It was my pleasure to assist, Jin. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
No, that's everything. Have a great day.

resolution_summary: Agent verified the account, acknowledged the policy constraint, and successfully processed a one-time exception refund along with a $10 courtesy credit.

judge_scores.justification: The agent verified account details appropriately while demonstrating strong empathy regarding the customer's travel circumstances. Furthermore, the agent correctly cited Section 4.2 of the refund policy and took proactive concrete action by securing a manual exception override and applying a courtesy credit.
